risks.description: The exception detail screen (esp. the static packet page, which renders a captured ReviewPayload) can show a state/next-action the backend no longer holds — e.g. NEEDS_REVIEW actions for a run already closed to DONE — because the page is built once and only the operator console re-reads live state.
risks.basis: AC-3 'the screen never shows a state the backend does not currently hold' (weight 3); build_review_payload gates on NEEDS_REVIEW while packet_page._render_packet_page renders a captured payload with no live state re-read.

risks.description: A next action is shown without naming who owns it, so the operator cannot tell that the decision is theirs (owner/operator) rather than something the system will do autonomously.
risks.basis: AC-1 'the exception detail screen names the next action and who owns it' (weight 3); action_options carry labels/consequences and client.operator_role='owner/operator' but ownership must be surfaced on the screen.

risks.description: The evidence the exception was raised from is missing, unresolved (mailbox:// sha that does not resolve is silently skipped in _copy_mailbox_evidence), or fabricated, leaving the operator unable to see why the exception fired.
risks.basis: AC-2 'the screen shows the evidence the exception was raised from' (weight 2); _evidence_links / _copy_mailbox_evidence drop links that cannot be bound.

risks.description: The screen change regresses the pilot site build or introduces a false-green in the render/reconciliation spine.
risks.basis: U-UI-11 touches review.py / packet_page.py / operator_console.py which the dogfood pilot and review tests exercise.

risks.description: The exception screen has no served HTTP route in the running product (8001 is the callback/Slack server), so operators may never actually reach the improved screen, or the static site can be served stale relative to the backend.
risks.basis: run_action_callback_server routes only /email/action,/actions/signed,/slack/*; the exception detail HTML is static site output (site:8000 per run_teammate), not served at the given app URL 8001.

scenarios.title: Exception detail names the next action and who owns it
scenarios.purpose: Confirm the review/exception payload that feeds the detail screen carries a concrete next action (action_options with label + consequence) and surfaces the accountable owner (owner/operator), not a bare status.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-UI-11: the exception detail screen names the next action and who owns it
scenarios.rationale: AC-1 has weight 3. The next-action + ownership logic lives in review._action_options_for and DogfoodClientProfile.operator_role; test_review_actions.py and test_review.py assert action options and operator_role, so a passing run is evidence the screen's inputs name the action and its owner.
setup: Repo checked out with .venv present (scripts/check_env.py green)
expected_observations: Suite passes: action_options exist with a concrete label and consequence for each exception outcome
operator_role resolves to owner/operator, i.e. the human who owns the next action is named
forbidden_observations: An exception outcome with zero action_options (no next action named)
A rendered next action with no owner/role attached
scenarios.isolation_note: Read-only: pytest fixtures build workflow stores in tempfiles and never touch data/active_workspace; no cleanup required.

scenarios.title: Exception detail shows the evidence it was raised from
scenarios.purpose: Confirm the exception detail payload carries the source evidence (carrier invoice + rate confirmation / received attachments) that triggered the exception, and that the text/render surface labels it as Evidence.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-UI-11: the screen shows the evidence the exception was raised from
scenarios.rationale: AC-2. test_review.py asserts evidence_links include carrier_invoice and rate_confirmation and that render_text contains an 'Evidence:' section; these are the exact inputs the packet page renders under its Evidence section.

actions.name: evidence-links-tests
actions.command: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -c pytest-canonical.ini eval/tests/test_review.py -q -k evidence or reason or payload

expected_observations: Evidence links for the exception include the documents the exception was raised from (carrier_invoice, rate_confirmation)
Text render includes an Evidence section listing those links
forbidden_observations: An exception payload with an empty evidence_links list
Evidence section rendered with a link to a document not tied to this load/exception
scenarios.isolation_note: Read-only pytest run using tempfile stores; no workspace mutation, no cleanup required.

scenarios.title: Missing/unlinked evidence still surfaces honestly, never fabricated
scenarios.purpose: When the exception's backing document cannot be linked (unlinked packet or unresolved mailbox sha), the screen must still show the received evidence honestly and must not invent a source document — verified via the pilot's packet-link accuracy.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-UI-11: the screen shows the evidence the exception was raised from
scenarios.rationale: _copy_mailbox_evidence silently skips mailbox:// links whose sha does not resolve and _render_unlinked_packet_page renders only payload evidence. test_pilot_session asserts packet_link_accuracy, the direct measure of whether rendered evidence links resolve to real artifacts rather than dead/fabricated ones.
expected_observations: packet_link_accuracy holds (rendered evidence/packet links resolve to real artifacts)
Unlinked exceptions render a 'Received Evidence' section rather than a broken canonical source doc
forbidden_observations: A rendered evidence link that points at a document the run never received
An unlinked exception rendered as if it had full source docs
scenarios.isolation_note: Read-only pilot tests build their site output under tempdirs; data/active_workspace untouched.

scenarios.title: No exception review UI for a run the backend has already closed
scenarios.purpose: A run that has left NEEDS_REVIEW (e.g. DONE) must not render an exception detail screen offering review actions or a NEEDS_REVIEW state — the render layer must reflect the current backend state only.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-UI-11: the screen never shows a state the backend does not currently hold
scenarios.rationale: AC-3 (weight 3). build_review_payload returns None unless run.state==NEEDS_REVIEW, and operator_console._review_card shows 'No active review actions; current state is <X>' when the live re-read differs. Running the review + pilot render tests exercises this gate; the DB check establishes that terminal states really do exist so the guard is load-bearing.

state_check.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT count(*) FROM workflow_runs WHERE state IN ('DONE','FAILED')"

expected_observations: Render/pilot tests pass: no review card / review actions are produced for runs not in NEEDS_REVIEW
workflow_runs contains terminal (DONE/FAILED) runs, proving the closed-run case is real
forbidden_observations: A review payload or action set produced for a run whose backend state is not NEEDS_REVIEW
sqlite error indicating the DB or table is missing
scenarios.isolation_note: pytest uses tempfile stores; the sqlite action is a read-only SELECT against the shared driver_probe DB and mutates nothing.

scenarios.title: Backend only ever holds a valid, closed set of states the screen can mirror
scenarios.purpose: Establish the ground truth AC-3 depends on: every persisted run holds exactly one state from the known WorkflowState enum and none is null/blank, so any state the screen displays can be checked against a real backend value.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-UI-11: the screen never shows a state the backend does not currently hold
scenarios.rationale: AC-3 is a screen-vs-backend agreement claim. Since the exception screen is static output with no served route at 8001, the executable half of the invariant is: the backend's own state column is well-formed and drawn only from the enum the render layer maps. A null/foreign state would mean the screen is showing something the backend cannot justify.

state_check.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT count(*) FROM workflow_runs WHERE state IS NULL OR state='' OR state NOT IN ('RECEIVED','EXTRACTED','RECONCILED','NEEDS_REVIEW','APPROVED','DISPUTED','REQUESTED_BACKUP','READY_FOR_ENTRY','ENTERING','ENTERED','DONE','FAILED','WAITING_FOR_SESSION')"

expected_observations: Query returns 0: no run holds a null, blank, or unknown state
The set of states the screen could render is fully backed by the enum
forbidden_observations: A nonzero count (a run whose persisted state is outside the known enum)
sqlite error indicating a missing DB/table
scenarios.isolation_note: Single read-only SELECT; no writes, no cleanup needed.

scenarios.title: Exception-screen change does not regress the pilot spine (no false green)
scenarios.purpose: Guard against the render change breaking reconciliation, review, delivery, or the dogfood site build, and against a silently-passing false-green.
scenarios.rationale: review.py / packet_page.py / operator_console.py sit on the pilot spine. The canonical suite plus run_diagnostics is the broadest regression signal available under the approved commands.
expected_observations: Full canonical suite passes with exit 0
forbidden_observations: Any failed/errored test in the canonical suite
scenarios.isolation_note: Canonical suite runs hermetically; run_diagnostics is a read/report script. Neither is expected to mutate data/active_workspace; if diagnostics writes a report artifact it is idempotent and self-contained.

assumptions: No builder diff, existing-coverage list, or prior-failure list was actually included in this prompt, so scenarios are grounded strictly in the three ACs, the product principles, and the code I read (review.py, packet_page.py, operator_console.py, workflow.py, run_action_callback_server.py).

The 'exception detail screen' is the generated static HTML in packet_page.py (packet/exception detail) plus operator_console.py (review-card grid); there is no live exception-detail HTTP endpoint on the callback server at http://127.0.0.1:8001.
data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 exists (it is named in an approved command) and contains the workflow_runs table with the WorkflowState enum values.
pytest fixtures for the review/pilot tests build their stores and site output in tempfiles and do not mutate data/active_workspace, so the pytest scenarios are effectively read-only.
The approved sqlite3 command accepts an inline SQL query as an extra argument (no shell operators).
unresolved_questions: Where is the improved exception detail screen actually served in the running product? The given app URL http://127.0.0.1:8001 is the callback/Slack server (routes: /email/action, /actions/signed, /slack/*) with no exception-detail HTML route; the static site is served at :8000 per run_teammate. Without a served route I cannot browser-verify the rendered screen against live backend state (the core of AC-3).

AC-3 enforcement asymmetry: operator_console._review_card re-reads live state and guards actions, but packet_page._render_packet_page renders a captured ReviewPayload with no live state re-read — does U-UI-11 require the packet detail page itself to reflect current backend state at view time, or is it acceptable for it to be a build-time snapshot? This determines whether a stale-state failure on the packet page is in scope.

Was any browser/UI-level test or served-page assertion added for U-UI-11? None was found (no test_operator_console.py; test_review.py does not assert 'names the owner' or the stale-state guard on the screen), so AC-1/AC-2/AC-3 appear to lack direct screen-level coverage and may need dedicated tests before the unit is trusted.

Which exact owner label must the screen show for the next action (e.g. 'owner/operator', a named person, or a role)? AC-1 requires naming who owns it but the requirement text does not fix the granularity, so I could not assert an exact string.
Do run_diagnostics.py / progress_status.py emit U-UI-11-specific signals I could assert on? Their output format was not confirmed, so S6 only checks exit status.
